newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA REVIEWS UNUTILISED MINERAL RIGHTS - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA REVIEWS UNUTILISED MINERAL RIGHTS - MINISTER.

text.p: The government was actively considering various ways in which South Africa's unutilised mineral rights could be used to create jobs and increase black ownership, Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday.
He told a media briefing that the mineral rights held by both government and the private sector were being reviewed.
Maduna said that he had told the Chamber of Mines that "we have to ensure that the mineral rights that are not being used now and which are in private hands, are also being used for development".

"We can't sit on them against the background of so much poverty and squalor and massive unemployment. Whatever resources the country has, in our opinion, ought to be tapped to improve the lives of our people."

Government was particularly committed to developing small-scale mining, he said. "We believe that it is going to enable us to bring particularly blacks and women into mining as holders of equity," Maduna added.
"We will have to look for all sorts of creative and innovative ways to do this because we accept that people do not have ready money to do this."

The development of small-scale mining was one issue the policy paper recently drafted by the parliamentary mining committee had not dealt with because of the hugely divergent views held by those affected, he said.
Some people wanted the state to control all mineral rights while others said they should all be privatised.

"There is a debate and at some point we will have to as a country bite the bullet and deal with that issue... because once you go beyond government there is a gross imbalance in the distribution of mineral rights and some are not being used right now," Maduna said.
He said that further discussions on the subject would be needed and he was studying what had been done in other countries, such as India.
